subject: Reserved commit anchoring & phased ramp — proposal and follow-ups
messages:

Subject: Reserved capacity options — initial questions

Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput looked great. We are trying to firm internal expectations for capacity procurement. A few things we need clarity on before legal/procurement will move:

- We are leaning toward a 24-month reserved commit but need a phased start: Novus will only be production-ready to consume ~40% of peak for the first 60–90 days while integration finishes. Can you outline how Redwood handles phased ramps and whether discounts are anchored to committed quantity or billing utilization?
- If you under-provision or miss throughput guarantees during our ramp, what credit/recourse do we get?
- Is there flexibility to convert unused commit in early months into credits for later months?

Also please attach any SOW draft and a sample term sheet we can pass to procurement.

—Pranav

Subject: Re: Reserved capacity options — initial questions

Hi Pranav — thanks for the clear questions. I attached a short needs assessment and a draft SOW (see attachments). High level response below; happy to hop on a call with procurement or legal to walk through specifics.

1) Phased ramps and anchoring
- We offer "anchored buckets": you pick a committed peak (e.g., 100 GPUs equivalent) and we define 3 ramp buckets (example: 40% for months 0–2, 70% for months 3–5, 100% thereafter). Discounts are applied to the committed capacity (so the unit price uses the committed tier) while billing reflects actual usage. This reduces price volatility while letting you start at lower utilization.

2) Throughput guarantees and credits
- We provide throughput SLOs per committed pool (tokens/sec and p99 latency targets). If we miss the SLO materially for a given month, we provide service credits applied to the invoice (formula in the term sheet) and automatic priority for remediation. For ramp months we cap the credit at a percentage of monthly commit value to avoid over-indexing against transient infra issues.

3) Converting early unused commit
- We can convert a portion of unused early-month commit into one-time account credits (subject to a floor and notice period). Alternatively, customers can elect to shift a percentage of future months forward (within the 24-month window) if there is clear justification.

Proposal attachments: Novus_Needs_Assessment.xlsx; Draft_SOW_Rev3.pdf

Suggested next steps: I can send a term sheet that shows three scenarios — 12/24/36 month commits — with the anchored-buckets ramp baked in and line-by-line economics. If procurement wants DocuSign-ready language, we can share that as well.

Proposed start date for a July production kick is July 1 — that gives us ~4 weeks for provisioning and onboarding.

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai

Sofia,

Procurement here — thanks for the quick note. A few clarifying items before we circulate to legal:

- In the anchored-buckets model, how are true-ups handled if utilization exceeds the upper bucket in month 4? Is there an automatic mid-term re-bill or an overage rate?
- If Novus elects to delay the second bucket (e.g., from month 3 to month 5) due to project delays, are we able to shift the ramp without penalty?
- Please confirm the maximum credit cap if Redwood misses a monthly throughput SLO — we need to know worst-case exposure.

Also please include a DocuSign link for a term sheet variant with a 24-month commit and the bucketed ramp reflected.

Thanks,
Novus Procurement
procurement@novushealth.com

Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Novus procurement questions — concession request

Team — forwarding procurement questions (see thread). Procurement is focused on three things: overage mechanics, ramp shifting flexibility, and max credit exposure. Pranav is pushing a 24-month commit but wants strong flexibility during the first 90 days.

Proposal for approval (commercial):
- Offer a 24-month reserved commit with anchored buckets: 40% (months 0–2), 70% (months 3–5), 100% (month 6 onward).
- Overage: bill at the committed unit price for the month if exceeded; if sustained >110% for 2 consecutive months, convert to a permanent increase with 30 days notice (protects us operationally).
- Ramp shifting: allow one scheduled shift of a bucket up to 60 days if notified 30 days before the scheduled increase.
- Credits cap: up to 20% of that month's commit value for missed throughput SLOs; escalate beyond that to commercial review.
- Concession: provide a one-time $25,000 onboarding credit if they sign within 14 days.

I think this is reasonable commercially and gives Novus the flexibility they want while protecting Redwood. If you approve, I will send the DocuSign link with the 24-month variant and those clauses.

Thoughts?
Sofia

Pranav / Angela — thanks for the back-and-forth. Based on internal review we can proceed with the following commercial terms for NovusHealth:

Summary — 24-month reserved commit (DEAL-5892)
- Committed peak: 100 GPU-equivalent units (example for clarity)
- Anchored ramp buckets: 40% (months 0–2), 70% (months 3–5), 100% (month 6 onward)
- Billing: billed on actual usage monthly; committed unit pricing applies to invoice calculations.
- Overage: usage above the month’s upper bucket billed at committed unit price; sustained >110% for two consecutive months triggers optional permanent adjustment (30 days notice).
- Ramp shifting: Novus may shift one scheduled bucket by up to 60 days provided Redwood receives a 30-day notice.
- Throughput SLO credits: up to 20% of monthly commit value for material SLO misses (details in term sheet). Larger remediation is handled through commercial review.
- Onboarding concession: one-time $25,000 credit on first invoice if signed within 14 calendar days of this email.
